title: Caldo Gallego
subtitle: Galician white bean and greens soup with pork
excerpt: Caldo gallego is the great soup of Galicia: a thick, sustaining broth of white beans, turnip greens, potatoes, and salt pork or chorizo. It is the everyday soup of the Galician countryside and one of the defining dishes of northwestern Spanish cooking. It is made in large pots and eaten throughout the week.
sourceNotes: Caldo gallego is the defining soup of Galicia, the green, rainy region of northwestern Spain. It is one of the most consumed soups in Spain and is central to Galician identity. The dish is mentioned in literature from the Middle Ages. Traditionally made with grelos (turnip greens), but cavolo nero or kale works well.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze without the greens. Add fresh greens when reheating.
recipe.batchNotes: Make a double batch. Improves over 2 to 3 days.

content.text: The traditional vegetable is grelos -- the leafy tops of turnips, which are widely grown in Galicia. Cavolo nero (black kale) or curly kale makes a very good substitute. The beans can be tinned for speed. If using dried beans, soak overnight and cook separately before adding to the soup.

items.prepNote: tough stems removed, leaves roughly torn

content.text: Heat {{extra-virgin-olive-oil}} oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add {{chorizo}} chorizo and cook for 3 minutes until starting to colour and release its red oil. Add {{onion}} onion and cook for 8 minutes. Add {{garlic}} garlic and {{smoked-paprika}} smoked paprika and cook for 1 minute.
Add {{potatoes-floury}} potatoes and 2 litres of water. Bring to a boil, season with {{salt-table}} salt and {{black-pepper}} pepper, and simmer for 20 minutes until the potatoes are almost tender.
Add {{cannellini-beans}} beans and {{cavolo-nero}} kale. Simmer for 15 minutes until the kale is tender. Taste for {{salt-table}} salt. Serve in deep bowls with crusty bread.

items.symptom: The soup is thin and watery
items.cause: Too much water, or the beans and potatoes haven't had enough time to soften.
items.fix: Mash a ladleful of potatoes and beans against the side of the pot and stir back in. This thickens the broth without adding anything extra.

content.text: Caldo gallego is the soup of Galicia, the green, wet region in the northwest of Spain that borders Portugal. Galicia has a distinct culinary identity shaped by its Atlantic coast and its Celtic heritage. The soup is made in every home across the region in winter and autumn. Galicians who emigrate take the soup with them -- it appears in Galician communities across South America and in Spanish restaurants around the world.
